1.title: Secure Access to Virtual Networks
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Secure Access to Virtual Networks. It covers the exam area Implement and manage virtual networking. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Create and configure network security groups (N S Gs) and application security groups. Evaluate effective security rules in N S Gs. Implement Azure Bastion. Configure service endpoints for Azure platform as a service. Configure private endpoints for Azure pass. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement and manage virtual networking (fifteen-twenty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Network security groups (NSGs)
1.text: Network security groups (N S Gs). An N S G is a list of allow and deny rules that filters inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources. Associate it with a subnet or a network interface (N I C). Priority. one hundred to four thousand ninety-six; lower number is processed first; processing stops at the first match. Source or destination. I P address, C I D R, service tag, or application security group. Protocol and port. T C P, U D P, I C M P, or Any; port or range. Action. Allow or Deny. Direction. Inbound or Outbound. Default rules (cannot be deleted, priority sixty-five thousand and above): Allow Vnet In Bound, Allow Azure Load Balancer In Bound, Deny All In Bound; outbound: Allow Vnet Out Bound, Allow Internet Out Bound, Deny All Out Bound.

1.title: Network security groups (NSGs), continued
1.text: Network security groups (N S Gs). The figure shows this: N S G rule evaluation: lowest priority number first, first match wins, with default rules at the end.

1.title: Network security groups (NSGs), continued
1.text: Network security groups (N S Gs). Service tags (for example Internet, Virtual Network, Storage, Azure Load Balancer ) stand for groups of I P prefixes that Microsoft maintains.

1.title: Application security groups (ASGs)
1.text: Application security groups (A S Gs). An A S G lets you group V Ms by role (web servers, database servers) and use the group as the source or destination in N S G rules, instead of I P addresses. Exam tip: "Allow web servers to reach database servers on port one thousand four hundred thirty-three without listing I P addresses" equals N S G rule between application security groups.

1.title: Effective security rules
1.text: Effective security rules. If both a subnet N S G and a N I C N S G exist, both are evaluated: inbound traffic passes the subnet N S G first, then the N I C N S G; outbound the reverse. Traffic must be allowed by both. Effective security rules (N I C blade). The combined result of all N S Gs on a N I C. I P flow verify. Allowed or denied for a given flow, and which rule.

1.title: Azure Bastion
1.text: Azure Bastion. Azure Bastion gives secure R D P and S S H to V Ms directly from the Azure portal over T L S (port four hundred forty-three), without public I P addresses on the V Ms. Subnet. A dedicated subnet named Azure Bastion Subnet, at least or twenty-six. S K Us. Developer, Basic, Standard, Premium with growing features. Benefit. No inbound R D P or S S H ports exposed to the internet. Exam tip: "Connect to V Ms by R D P or S S H securely with no public I P s and no open ports" equals Azure Bastion.

1.title: Service endpoints and private endpoints
1.text: Service endpoints and private endpoints. The figure shows this: A service endpoint compared with a private endpoint for reaching an Azure pass service.

1.title: Service endpoints and private endpoints, continued
1.text: Service endpoints and private endpoints. What it is. Service endpoint: Extends the V net identity to the service over the Azure backbone. Private endpoint: A network interface with a private I P in your V net that maps to one instance of the service. Service I P. Service endpoint: Still the service's public I P. Private endpoint: A private I P from your subnet. Reach from on-premises. Service endpoint: No. Private endpoint: Yes, through V P N (virtual private network) or Express Route.

1.title: Service endpoints and private endpoints, continued
1.text: Service endpoints and private endpoints. D N S. Service endpoint: No change. Private endpoint: Needs a private D N S zone (for example privatelink dot blob dot core dot windows dot net ). Cost. Service endpoint: Free. Private endpoint: Charged (per endpoint and data). Use. Service endpoint: Simple, free subnet restriction. Private endpoint: Fully private access, data exfiltration protection. Exam tip: On-premises access over a private connection, or a private I P for the pass service equals private endpoint. Subnet-only restriction at no cost equals service endpoint.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Two N S G rules apply to the same traffic: priority two hundred allows it and priority three hundred denies it. What is the result? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Allowed, because the lower number is processed first. Rules are processed from the lowest priority number and the first match wins.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Web servers must be allowed to reach database servers on one port without using I P addresses. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Application security groups in N S G rules. A S Gs group V Ms by role for use in rules.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Administrators need R D P and S S H to V Ms that have no public I P s and no open inbound ports. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Bastion. Bastion provides T L S-based access from the portal.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What is the required name for the Azure Bastion subnet? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Bastion Subnet. The dedicated subnet must be named Azure Bastion Subnet.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An on-premises network must reach an Azure storage account over a private connection. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A private endpoint. Private endpoints are reachable from on-premises through V P N or Express Route.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A V M has an N S G on both its subnet and its N I C. What must be true for inbound traffic to reach it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Both N S Gs must allow it. Traffic is evaluated by both N S Gs.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What decides which N S G rule applies first? Answer: The lowest priority number. Question two. Name one default inbound N S G rule. Answer: For example Allow Vnet In Bound or Deny All In Bound. Question three. What does an application security group do? Answer: Groups V Ms by role for use in N S G rules.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What port does Bastion use from the browser? Answer: four hundred forty-three over T L S. Question five. Which endpoint type gives a private I P in your V net? Answer: A private endpoint. Question six. What D N S setup does a private endpoint need? Answer: A private D N S zone for the service.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. N S G: priority one hundred to four thousand ninety-six, first match wins, default rules, service tags, subnet or N I C. A S G: group V Ms by role for rules. Effective rules: subnet and N I C N S Gs both apply; I P flow verify. Bastion: Azure Bastion Subnet or twenty-six, R D P or S S H over T L S, no public I P. Endpoints: service endpoint (free, public I P of service) versus private endpoint (private I P, on-premises reach, private D N S).
